title: Pro-étale inverse image along a site object is slice restriction
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme, $A$ a commutative ring, and $r\colon W\to X$ a morphism of schemes such that $W\xrightarrow{r}X$ is an object of the small pro-étale site $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Identify $W_{\mathrm{proét}}$ with the localization $X_{\mathrm{proét}}/W$ by the equivalence of [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization], and for a sheaf $G$ of sets, of abelian groups or of $A_X$-modules on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ write $G|_W$ for its restriction, $G|_W(U\to W)=G(U\to W\xrightarrow{r}X)$, with the restriction maps of $G$. Let $u_r$, the presheaf inverse image $u_{r,p}$, the inverse image $r^{-1}=(u_{r,p}-)^\#$, the structure map $c^r_A\colon r^{-1}A_X\to A_W$ and the module pullback $r^*G=r^{-1}G\otimes_{r^{-1}A_X}A_W$ be those of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], with $A_X,A_W$ the constant sheaves of rings [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Then:

1. For every object $U\to W$ of $W_{\mathrm{proét}}$, the pair $(U\to W\xrightarrow{r}X,\ \varphi_0)$ with $\varphi_0=(\mathrm{str},\mathrm{id}_U)\colon U\to W\times_XU=u_r(U\to X)$ is an initial object of the indexing category $\mathcal I_U$ of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Consequently the coprojections indexed by these pairs give an isomorphism of presheaves $G|_W\xrightarrow{\sim}u_{r,p}G$, natural in $G$, and the canonical map $u_{r,p}G\to r^{-1}G$ to the sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] is an isomorphism; thus $r^{-1}G\cong G|_W$ naturally in $G$, for sheaves of sets, of abelian groups and of rings.
2. Under this identification $r^{-1}A_X\cong A_X|_W$, the structure map $c^r_A$ is a ring isomorphism $A_X|_W\to A_W$, namely the inverse of the isomorphism $A_W\to A_X|_W$ of clause (2) of [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization].
3. For every sheaf $G$ of $A_X$-modules there is an isomorphism of sheaves of $A_W$-modules $r^*G\cong G|_W$, natural in $G$, where $G|_W$ is an $A_W$-module through the isomorphism of (2); in particular the underlying abelian sheaf of $r^*G$ is that of $G|_W$.

source.place: Tag 03CE (lemma-localize-given-products): for $U\in\mathcal C$ with products of pairs, $v(X)=X\times U/U$ defines the morphism of sites $\mathcal C/U\to\mathcal C$ whose topos morphism is $j_U$ (inverse image = restriction); applied to the base-change functor of proetale.tex Tag 09A5. Pro-étale analogue of the DAG node lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction (étale case).

proof.text: By clause (1) of [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization], composition with $r$ identifies $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with $X_{\mathrm{proet}}/W$, including its coverings. In particular the composite $U\to X$ is an object of the ambient site. By [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], restriction of a sheaf to this slice is a sheaf, with value $G(U)$ at $U\to W$, for sets, abelian groups, rings and modules over the restricted ring. We use this identification throughout. There is no requirement that $r$ be an open immersion or a monomorphism.

source.place: Tag 00XZ (section-localize), definition-localize and the restriction formula following it; applied to the site equivalence in the cited localization lemma.

proof.text: Fix $U\xrightarrow{s}W$. The pair $t_U=(U\to X,\varphi_0)$ is an object of $\mathcal I_U$ of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], because $\varphi_0=(s,\mathrm{id}_U):U\to W\times_XU$ is a $W$-morphism. For any $(V,\varphi)$ in $\mathcal I_U$, put $a_\varphi=\mathrm{pr}_V\varphi:U\to V$. This is an $X$-morphism. The maps $u_r(a_\varphi)\varphi_0$ and $\varphi$ have the same projections $s$ and $a_\varphi$, so are equal by [def-pc-fibre-product]. Thus $a_\varphi$ is an arrow $t_U\to(V,\varphi)$. Conversely any such arrow $a$ satisfies $a=\mathrm{pr}_V\varphi$ after applying the second projection to its defining equality. This proves initiality, including uniqueness, directly from the indexing-category definition.

source.place: Tag 03CE (lemma-localize-given-products), proof of the adjunction by the product universal property; Tag 00VC (section-functoriality-PSh), equation-colim-category.

proof.text: Use exactly the colimit over $\mathcal I_U^{\mathrm{op}}$ specified by [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], in each of sets, abelian groups and rings. Write $i_{V,\varphi}:G(V)\to(u_{r,p}G)(U)$ for its coprojections and $\alpha_U=i_{t_U}$. For an indexing arrow $b:(V,\varphi)\to(V',\varphi')$ we have $a_{\varphi'}=b a_\varphi$, hence $G(a_{\varphi'})=G(a_\varphi)G(b)$. The maps $G(a_\varphi):G(V)\to G(U)$ therefore form a cocone and give $\beta_U:(u_{r,p}G)(U)\to G(U)$ with $\beta_U i_{V,\varphi}=G(a_\varphi)$. Since $a_{\varphi_0}=\mathrm{id}_U$, $\beta_U\alpha_U=\mathrm{id}$. The colimit relation for $a_\varphi:t_U\to(V,\varphi)$ is $\alpha_U G(a_\varphi)=i_{V,\varphi}$; checking on all coprojections gives $\alpha_U\beta_U=\mathrm{id}$. This proves the colimit comparison without assuming arbitrary ring colimits are computed on underlying sets.

source.place: Tag 00VC (section-functoriality-PSh), colimit definition and its coprojections; Tag 03CE (lemma-localize-given-products).

proof.text: For a $W$-morphism $b:U'\to U$, the restriction rule of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] sends $i_{V,\varphi}$ to $i_{V,\varphi b}$. Since $a_{\varphi b}=a_\varphi b$, the maps $\beta_U$ commute with restriction: on each coprojection both composites are $G(b)G(a_\varphi)$. Thus $\beta:u_{r,p}G\to G|_W$ and its inverse $\alpha$ are presheaf morphisms. A morphism $h:G\to H$ satisfies $h_U G(a_\varphi)=H(a_\varphi)h_V$, so the same coprojection check proves naturality in $G$. In particular these comparisons preserve all operations whenever the values carry abelian-group or ring structures.

source.place: Tag 00VC (section-functoriality-PSh), restriction maps on coprojections; Tag 03CE (lemma-localize-given-products).

proof.text: By steps 1 and 4, $P=u_{r,p}G$ is already a sheaf. Let $q:P\to P^\#$ be the canonical map of [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Its universal property extends $\mathrm{id}_P$ uniquely to $e:P^\#\to P$, with $eq=\mathrm{id}_P$. The maps $qe$ and $\mathrm{id}_{P^\#}$ agree after precomposition with $q$, so uniqueness gives $qe=\mathrm{id}_{P^\#}$. Thus $q$ is an isomorphism. The definition $r^{-1}G=P^\#$ in [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] and the isomorphism $\alpha:G|_W\to P$ give clause (1), naturally in $G$, for each stated category of values.

We verify the particular structure map, not merely the existence of a ring isomorphism. Write $R=A_X|_W$ and let $e:A_W\to R$ be the ring isomorphism in clause (2) of [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization]. Under step 5 let $d:R\to A_W$ be $c_A^r$. Its definition in [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] is adjunction applied to $\rho:A_X\to r_*A_W$. Explicitly, its composite with the coprojection at $(V,\varphi)$ is $A_W(\varphi)\rho_V$: these maps form a cocone by naturality of $\rho$, are natural in $U$, and their value at $(V,\mathrm{id}_{u_r(V)})$ recovers $\rho_V$, which is the defining adjunction correspondence: by [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-functor-sheaf-pullback-adjunction] the bijection is the composite of $u_p\dashv u^p$, whose unit at $V$ is the coprojection at $(V,\mathrm{id}_{u_r(V)})$, and of sheafification. At $t_U$ this is $A_W(\varphi_0)\rho_U$, and it sends the constant section $a$ to $a$, since $\rho$ does so by definition. The map $e$ also sends constant sections to themselves. Therefore $de:A_W\to A_W$ agrees with the identity on the constant presheaf. Since $A_W$ is its sheafification [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], uniqueness in [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] gives $de=\mathrm{id}$. As $e$ is an isomorphism, $d=e^{-1}$, proving clause (2).

source.place: Tag 03CE (lemma-localize-given-products) and Tag 0H7J (example-constant-sheaf); structure map via the adjunction of Tag 00VC (section-functoriality-PSh).

proof.text: Let $G$ be an $A_X$-module sheaf. The comparison of steps 3-5 on its underlying abelian sheaf identifies $r^{-1}G$ with $M=G|_W$. This identifies its $r^{-1}A_X$-action with the original $R=A_X|_W$-action: by [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] the inverse-image action is obtained from the original action map by the finite-product comparison. Evaluate both factors at the distinguished pair $t_U$. The comparison sends a pair $(a,m)\in A_X(U)\times G(U)$ to the pair of their distinguished coprojections, and the image of the action sends it to the coprojection of $am$. Consequently the identified action is $(a,m)\mapsto am$. This holds at every object and commutes with restrictions by step 4, and with module homomorphisms by its naturality.

source.place: Tag 03D2 (lemma-pullback-module), in literature/stacks-project/sites-modules.tex: action by applying inverse image to the multiplication map and its product comparison.

proof.text: Give $M=G|_W$ its $A_W$-action through $d^{-1}:A_W\to R$, where $d:R\to A_W$ is step 6. By [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] and [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], $r^*G$ is the sheafification of $U\mapsto M(U)\otimes_{R(U)}A_W(U)$. Define on this presheaf $m\otimes a\mapsto d_U^{-1}(a)m$, with inverse $m\mapsto m\otimes1$. Balancing proves the first map well defined. Their composites are identities: one gives $m$, the other sends $m\otimes a$ to $d_U^{-1}(a)m\otimes1=m\otimes a$. Both are $A_W(U)$-linear, commute with restrictions, and commute with homomorphisms in $G$. Thus this tensor presheaf is already isomorphic to the sheaf $M$. By the universal property of sheafification of presheaves of modules [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], as in step 5, its sheafification is $M$. This proves the natural $A_W$-module isomorphism of clause (3), and hence the assertion on underlying abelian sheaves.
